meta.title: The Tortoise and the Stars
meta.textType: story: a poem with repeated words

paragraphs: Lily and Tom stayed with Grandpa and Grandma in Green Hill on Saturday. The weather was hot, and the garden was dry. The grass was brown, and there was no rain for many days. "Look!" said Lily. "Something is under the big leaf." It was a tortoise with a round brown shell. "Is it a boy or a girl?" asked Tom. "Nobody knows," said Grandpa with a smile.

"It looks like a small dinosaur," said Tom. "When I was small, I had a tortoise," said Grandpa. "Tortoises are very old animals, like dinosaurs." The tortoise walked slowly across the dry grass. Pip ran next to it, but he did not touch it. "We are lucky," said Grandma. "It does not come to our garden every day." Lily gave the tortoise a little water in a small bowl.

In the evening, they sat on the step in front of the house. The sky was dark, and many stars came out. The air was cool now, and the garden was very quiet. "I have a poem for you," said Grandpa. "Say the words after me." "Star, star, star, up in the sky." "Star, star, star, we say good night." "Slow, slow, slow, the tortoise walks." "Slow, slow, slow, the garden talks." Lily and Tom said the poem two times.

Then Pip put his head on Lily's knee and closed his eyes. "Pip is ready to sleep," said Tom. Grandma gave them each a warm blanket, and Grandpa smiled at the children. In the dark garden, the tortoise was still there. "Good night, tortoise," whispered Lily. "Good night, stars."
text.summary: Lily and Tom visit Grandpa and Grandma in Green Hill. They see a tortoise in the dry garden, and in the evening Grandpa says a poem about the tortoise and the stars.
